string.text: The .45 calibre full metal jacket round has enjoyed popularity for a hundred years thanks to its ballistic performance and a relatively small propelling charge. As a result, the bullet in this round is relatively slow but highly accurate and provides considerable stopping power.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:
This unusual .45 ACP calibre round consists of a jacketed soft point bullet with a hollow steel core, possessing both their advantages and disadvantages.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 12.7x55 mm SC-130 is a Russian rifle cartridge with a subsonic bullet, developed by TsKIB SOO for quiet, flashless engagement of protected targets and personnel wearing heavy body armor at ranges of up to 600 m.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

A standard 12-gauge cartridge loaded with 9 mm buckshot. It has enormous lethal and stopping power at medium and close range. Intended for smoothbore weapons and shotguns.
 
%c[ui_gray_1]SPECIAL FEATURE:

A homemade 12-gauge cartridge loaded with 6 mm shot. Extremely effective at close range. It can be used only in smoothbore weapons and shotguns.

12 gauge custom-made slugs for putting down dinosaurs and mutants. Slug inside is made of lead covered in copper that has steel, dart-like insert inside. Slug is very long and has got big powder load. It really can break your hands with recoil.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

A hand-assembled 12-gauge cartridge, loaded with the expanding ‘Impuls-8’ bullet and an increased powder charge. The ‘Impuls-8’ bullet has an expanding jacket with a steel ball core. On the ‘mainland’, such cartridges are not used because there is no point (since anything made of flesh is turned into mince after a hit); in the Zone, however, this ammunition is highly valued for hunting the most dangerous mutants. Excellent ballistic performance combined with exceptional stopping power. Its drawbacks are a very high price and increased weapon wear. The bullet’s steel core can penetrate a medium-class bulletproof vest\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

This heavy 12 gauge slug round is normally used for hunting big game, but is also good for other purposes. Instead of piercing, this hefty slug simply crushes through armour.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The .338 Lapua Magnum is a specialised rimless bottlenecked centrefire cartridge developed for military long-range sniper rifles. The Afghanistan War and Iraq War made it a combat-proven round with ready and substantial ammunition availability. The .338 Lapua is a dual-purpose anti-personnel and anti-materiel round, but its anti-materiel potential is limited.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The .357 HP round is a hollow-point bullet. The purpose of the round is to slow down upon impact, which decreases its penetration, but at the same time causes larger internal tissue damage.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The HK 4.6?30mm cartridge is a type of ammunition primarily used in the Heckler & Koch MP7 Personal defense weapon (PDW). It is designed to minimize weight and recoil while increasing penetration of body armor. It features a bottlenecked case and a pointed, steel-core, brass-jacketed bullet.

Military 5.45x39 calibre 7N22 armour-piercing round for automatic rifles of Warsaw Pact countries. The bullet contains a hard-alloy armour-piercing penetrator. Effective against body armour.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7N10 military cartridge in 5.45x39 mm, loaded with an increased-penetration (EP) bullet, is used in automatic rifles of many Warsaw Pact member states. The bullet’s heat-treated steel core provides improved target penetration.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

Military 5.45x39 calibre 7N6 was the first standard issue round for automatic rifles of Warsaw Pact countries using the new intermediate cartridge. Provides better accuracy than the 7.62 calibre round thanks to reduced recoil and a 100-metre increase in range.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

Known by the designation M855A1, this 5.56x45 mm Enhanced Performance Round is the latest cartridge used by the US Army. The bullet consists of a copper semi-jacket with a steel tip, travels at a higher velocity, and penetrates armor better than the SS109/M855 bullet. It is more effective against both enemy armor and soft tissue.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

A standard-issue NATO 5.56x45 calibre M193 round specially designed for accurate automatic fire. Provides good ballistic characteristics, having been designed on the basis of a hunting round. Well known for being used in the Vietnam war and having great performance against tissue, but limited penetration.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

Standard NATO military cartridge in 5.56x45 mm, known by the designation M855, with a steel core. Despite causing less damage to soft tissue, this cartridge has increased penetration.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 5.7x28 mm SS190 cartridge was developed by the Belgian company Fabrique Nationale specifically for the FN P90 submachine gun in the mid-1980s. It was later used in the Five-seveN pistol. It has greater penetration than other pistol cartridges. Its bullet reaches a muzzle velocity of up to 716 m/s and can pierce body armor. Its stopping power is three times that of the 9x19 mm cartridge.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:
The 5.7x28 mm cartridge known as SS195LF has an expanding bullet. Its penetration is lower than that of SS190, but its stopping power and lethality are greater.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

.50 BMG (12.7x99 mm) is a large-caliber cartridge created in the 1920s for the Browning M1921 (M2HB) heavy machine gun. During World War II it was in service with all Allied countries and was used mainly in aircraft machine guns. It was also supplied to the USSR with Lend-Lease armored vehicles and aircraft.
After World War II, .50 BMG spread worldwide, except in Warsaw Pact countries, as NATO’s standard heavy-caliber infantry machine-gun cartridge. Today, more than 30 manufacturers produce it to US standards. The cartridge has several variants: M2 ball, M2 armor-piercing, M8 armor-piercing incendiary, M1 incendiary, and M1 tracer. Ammunition for sustained bursts is linked into belts.
The cartridge is also used in heavy-caliber sniper rifles.

A Soviet 7.62 mm pistol cartridge, now known as the 7.62x25 mm Tokarev. Its bullet has a lead core and a steel jacket plated with tombac. Muzzle velocity is 420 m/s and energy is 510 J. To secure the bullet more reliably in its brass case, the case mouth was circumferentially crimped and then rolled. Large stocks of these cartridges still remain in depots of Russian Armed Forces units.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The steel core 7.62x25mm cartridge is a Russian bottle-necked pistol cartridge widely used in former Soviet satellite states, China and Pakistan among other countries. It’s very effective against unarmoured targets.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

7.62x39 M43 is an armour piercing round produced in China, which is why it’s often referred to as "7.62x39 CN". This round features a mild steel core which enhances its penetration capabilities. This Chinese round (as well as all other M43 ammunition) is currently banned for import in the US because US federal law classifies the round as an armour-piercing handgun round. This classification is based on materials and bullet design rather than on empirical ability to penetrate armour.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

7.62x39 Full Metal Jacket is one the most commonly used types of ammunition, especially in Africa and in the Middle East. Some nicknamed it the "Round of the Revolution" due to its favored use by both terrorist and criminal organizations. Due to the sheer power of the round most military organizations have turned to using additional steel plates to counter 7.62x39 as there is a high probability of encountering it in combat situations.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:
Military 7.62x51 calibre M61 armor-piercing round with a hardened steel core. It retains high damage while greatly improving performance against body armor.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7.62x51 NATO round is a military variant of the .308 round which was used as a standard-issue by the NATO forces until 5.56 ammunition was introduced in the ’70s in the Vietnam War. At present, it is most commonly employed by private military contractors all over the world. The 7.62x51 round is a very common machine gun calibre, and can also be used in battle or sniper rifles.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

A 7.62x54 calibre sniper round with a steel penetrator specially designed for the SVD. It’s steel core is made to pierce light armors. Very common in the zone, these bullets are quite cheap.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The inexpensive 7N13 armor-piercing machine-gun cartridge in 7.62x54 mm. Due to its design, it is unsuitable for firing from sniper rifles, so it is used as ammunition for the PKM machine gun. This cartridge has increased power and, thanks to its steel core, very good penetration. A powerful cartridge for a powerful weapon.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7.62x54 PP is a dated rifle calibre introduced in the Soviet Empire at the turn of the 19th century and was still used by the USSR after World War II. It was originally designed for the Mosin-Nagant standard-issue infantry rifle and is quite common in the Zone due to the popularity of the rifle. The round is relatively cheap (considering it comes in boxes of 50) but has surprisingly good penetrative capabilities, even in comparison to more modern ammo types. It can also be used as a cheaper solution in the PKM machine gun.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The specially developed, modernized 7.62x54 mm sniper cartridge uses the armor-piercing 7N14 bullet. The bullet has a combined core made of lead and hardened U12A-grade steel, capable of penetrating body armor and small obstacles. Compared with a standard cartridge of the same caliber, it has a lighter tail section, which provides greater accuracy and improved ballistic characteristics.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7.92x57 PS round was used by the British armed forces against armored targets. Its hardened steel core gives it high penetration. Primarily used for long-range shooting, it is of higher quality than the standard round. It is used in some sniper rifles.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7.92x57 Mauser round was adopted by the German Empire and then the Third Reich. It was one of the most popular cartridges in the period of two world wars. However, nowadays, the round is primarily used for hunting and sports.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

RG028 is a cartridge used for its armour penetration capabilities. The goal of the RG028 was to become a counter to body armour; for this reason, it’s loaded with a hardened steel core. Unfortunately, the round itself isn’t much of an improvement over the standard, it just has a stronger impact than typical 9x18 round.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:
A full metal jacket round with a steel penetrator and a lead core under a metal jacket. Provides good stopping power but is ineffective against body armour.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 7N16 round has enhanced stopping power. The European +P+ marking means very high chamber pressure. Its bullet travels 30% faster than a standard round. It is ineffective against body armor.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The 9x19 mm armor-piercing cartridge has a bullet with a steel core. It was developed to improve the penetration capability of pistols and submachine guns. It is used mainly by anti-terrorist and special police units when facing opponents protected by body armor.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

This basic 9x19 calibre round with a jacketed bullet has good characteristics while being simple to produce. The round is popular due to the fact that international conventions prohibit the use of expanding ammunition in combat. Ineffective against body armour.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

This 9x19 calibre jacketed hollow-point bullet with an expanding hollow has high stopping power and low ricochet propensity. Used by police and for self-defense. Ineffective against body armour due to its low penetration potential, but flesh damage. One of the cheapest ammo to efficiently kill mutants in the zone.\n \n%c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:

The SP-6 is a subsonic armour-piercing round with a jacketed soft point bullet with a hard steel core that protrudes from the casing. Requires a suppressor for stealth firing. Used by special services of Warsaw Pact countries. Effective against light body armour.

The SP-5 is a subsonic rifle round with a bimetallic casing. The round contains a steel core with a gap behind it that is filled with lead. Requires a suppressor for stealth firing. Used by special services of Warsaw Pact countries.

The large-caliber SC-130 VPS (high penetration capability) sniper cartridge is designed to silently engage enemy personnel protected by heavy body armor (protection level 5–6 under GOST R50744-95) at ranges of up to 200 meters, or personnel behind various obstacles (vehicle bodywork, a door, glass, a fence, etc.) at ranges of up to 600 meters. It is also intended to engage lightly armored and unarmored vehicles.\n \n %c[ui_gray_1]PARAMETERS:
